plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record is frozen against all gradient/near-max/spike/grid moves tried on it (F288, F365-F372, F376, p0405/p0441/p0444/p0445 all flat), so the main slot should stop polishing and use a non-local, target-driven move: least-squares refit of h to a prescribed f*f shape. R = ||L||_2^2/(L_1*L_max), so the only useful reshapings raise the low knots of L while not raising the max; a projected-Landweber fit to a flat/soft-clipped target does exactly that and has never been tried. T21 has one live, uniquely validated lever (forced rank pruning, F373, +6e-6, zero fraction 19.5->35%), which should be pushed further at its current 169984 grid rather than re-gridded. For the backtrack, p0209 is the clean N=42496 sharp optimum on the record lineage; only 2x staircase doubling was ever tried from this family, so non-integer (1.25x/1.5x/1.75x) mass-preserving upsampling is genuine new sub-cell freedom.

experiments.hypothesis: R is limited by the tall f*f peak (L_max/mean ~1.93) while 57% of knots sit well below the max. Every gradient surrogate so far only nudged the argmax; a projected least-squares refit of h against an explicit flat / soft-clipped target moves mass globally in one shot (peak down, flanks up), a direction first-order polish cannot take because it needs simultaneous multi-knot change.
experiments.change: From start=p0405 (N=84992, rescale first). Build L = knots(h). For each target family and parameter: (A) flat targets T = c*ones(n+1) with sum(T) set equal to sum(L), c = 1.0, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5 x mean(L); (B) soft-clip targets T = sum(L)/sum(L - lam*max(L-q*Lmax,0)) * (L - lam*max(L - q*Lmax,0)) with q in {0.90,0.95,0.98}, lam in {0.5,1.0}. For each T run projected Landweber on h: h <- clip(h - eta * 2*corr(h, (h*h - T)), 0, None) with eta = 0.4/(4*max(h)+1e-12) for 40 iterations, rescale (h/sqrt(max knots)), then sharp log-space L-BFGS 120 iters (_lbfgs_log) and peak-window polish (+-0.10N, 120 iters). Keep a candidate only if R_of rises above the running best; print R after each (family,param). Spend all remaining time cycling the best two parameters with sharp + p-norm (p=8,32,128) polish in the peak window until ~2 s before the deadline, then final full-space sharp polish. Return best-by-exact-R (start if nothing beats it).
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.941260 (+1.7e-5 over the record). Signature of success: exact R rises for at least one clip/flat parameter while L_max/mean falls below 1.93 and the 0.1%-near-max knot fraction rises above 18.24% (peak traded for flank mass). If every target refit lands at or below 0.941243 even after sharp polish, the record's L-shape is locally L2-optimal at fixed L_max and the whole target-refit family is dead on this construction.

experiments.hypothesis: F373's lever (hard rank pruning + sharp polish) was only swept to q=0.45 and stopped climbing at 169984 with 35% zeros, so the q-ladder is likely truncated, not exhausted. Pushing q to 0.55/0.65 and pruning asymmetrically (only in the half containing the f*f argmax at 0.407) changes which knots the gradient can reach and should keep lifting the track's own best; this is T21's validated direction, not the record's.
experiments.change: From start=p0443 (N=169984, 35.0% zeros, Lmax at 0.407 of support). (1) Symmetric ladder: for q in {0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65} zero the smallest-q fraction of cells by height, _rescale, sharp _lbfgs_log 120 iters on active cells, then peak-window polish (window +-0.08N around argmax(L), 100 iters); record exact R_of. (2) Asymmetric ladder on the best two: zero smallest-q fraction only within the half that contains argmax(L) (q in {0.20,0.35,0.50} of that half) and in the opposite half separately, same polish. (3) On the best candidate, one far-tail revival pass: exact zeros inside [0,0.12N) and [0.88N,N) set to 1e-3 * local 1024-cell mean, sharp 60 iters, keep only on exact-R gain. (4) Remaining time: alternate sharp (150 it) and p-norm (p=4,16,64, 100 it) polishes on the best, printing R, zero fraction, max/mean and near-max fraction after each stage. Return best-by-exact-R.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.940480 (+2.4e-5 over the track best 0.940456). Signature: the q-ladder peaks at q in 0.50-0.60 with zero fraction rising toward 40-45% and max/mean rising from 97.1, with the 0.1%-near-max fraction above 17.55%; asymmetric pruning beating symmetric pruning would show the argmax side is the binding constraint. If R declines monotonically past q=0.45, T21's sparsity is saturated at 35% and this track has no further lever.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record basin is saturated: 29 documented failures on that construction (warps, block/immediate refinement, bumps, variance penalties, resolution splits). The strongest unexhausted object is p0425 (0.941217, N=84992, distinct basin with f*f argmax at 0.563 vs record 0.338), which was produced by doubling and has never had a full-budget polish of its own. T25's block model collapsed to the smooth max/mean 2.02 basin because its seeds were not extreme enough to encode a sub-cell spike; that family deserves one honest spiky-seed test. T26's Gaussian-bump attempt died on a TypeError before running, and F391's bump fit was done at N=2048, which cannot represent a one-cell spike at N=84992; full-resolution bump fitting is genuinely untested.

experiments.hypothesis: p0425 is a high-resolution (N=84992) local optimum in a different basin from the record (f*f argmax 0.563 vs 0.338) and has never received a full p-norm/sharp/peak polish in its own right; its doubling step gave only +4e-6, so a full 60 s polish on its own landscape can plausibly gain more than the 2.6e-5 needed to pass 0.941243.
experiments.change: From start (= p0425, N=84992). Do not pre-perturb. (a) Run a p-norm homotopy p = 8,16,32,64,128, each 250 L-BFGS iterations in log-height space on the active set with _fun_grad_pnorm; after every two p-stages run a sharp _fun_grad L-BFGS (250 it) followed by peak-window polish (200 it) over the union of windows around every knot within 0.5% of the current max, each window +/- max(64, 0.02*N). (b) Then repeat until deadline-2 s: pick a random subset of the top 2% tallest cells, multiply them by exp(N(0,0.03)), re-run sharp + peak polish, and accept the perturbed result only if exact R_of improves by >1e-13. (c) Finish with a 400-iteration sharp polish before returning. Use fftconvolve exclusively; no N-by-N arrays.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.941250 (+3.3e-5 over the start, +7e-6 over the record), stretch 0.94127. Signature: the p=32/64/128 stages gain at least 1e-6, and the fraction of f*f knots within 0.1% of max rises above p0425's 17.92% while Lmax/mean falls. If every stage is flat, p0425 is a hard local optimum and the basin is closed.

experiments.hypothesis: p0462's block model reached only the smooth max/mean 2.02 basin because its seed heights (a_k in [3,6], rest in [-2,0]) were far too mild and it never forced a sub-cell spike or exact zeros. With one gap of width ~1e-3 (sub-cell at N=1024), a dominant block at height exp(10-16), an adjacent shoulder, and 30-60% of blocks exactly zero, the same continuous-edge rasterization should reach the spiky compact spike+plateau regime and beat the track's 0.842660.
experiments.change: From start (= p0462). Keep p0462's continuous-edge softmax-gap rasterizer, fftconvolve R, and escalation code. Replace the seed generator: for K in {10,16,24}, make 10 restarts each with (i) one spike gap log-uniform in [1e-3, 1/K^2], (ii) the remaining K-1 gaps log-uniform in [0.02, 3/K], (iii) spike log-height a=U(10,16), 1-2 shoulder blocks adjacent to the spike with a=U(2,5), all other blocks a=U(-8,0), and (iv) a random 30-60% of non-spike blocks forced to a=-30 (exact zero after exp clipping). Optimize (z,a) with Powell at N=1024, maxfev 1200, each restart hard-capped at 1.0 s; keep the top 5 by exact R. Escalate the top 3 by exact duplication 1024->2048->4096->8192->16384->32768, at each level running sharp log-height L-BFGS (120 it), p-norm p=8 and p=32 (60 it each), then a 5%-wide peak-window polish; stop escalating a seed if its R drops more than 0.02 below the best seed's R at that level. Leave 2 s margin and return the best.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.88 at N=32768 (beat 0.842660 by >0.03; stretch 0.90 and beat T22's 0.863873). Signature: at least one seed reaches max/mean > 15 with R > 0.78 at N=1024 before escalation, and the final f*f argmax is off-centre with >5% of knots within 1% of max. If all seeds stay at max/mean < 5, the constant-block family is structurally too smooth and the track should switch to piecewise-linear block profiles.

experiments.hypothesis: F391 failed because it fitted a Gaussian-bump model at N=2048 and then rasterized, which erases the record's one-cell spike (max/mean 147). Evaluating the bump model directly at full N=84992, seeded from the record's own mass clusters and with the spike represented by a sigma ~ 0.5 cell bump, gives a continuous-position parameterization that can move the spike and plateau off the grid and break the staircase local optimum that all height-space moves are stuck in.
experiments.change: From start (= p0405, N=84992). Build h_i = sum_{m=1..M} exp(a_m) exp(-(x_i-c_m)^2/(2 s_m^2)) with M=16, x_i=(i+0.5)/N, c_m in [0,1] (logit parameterization), log s_m in [log(0.3/N), log(0.15)], log a_m in [-20,20]. Initialize by greedy mass matching: take the current h, find the cell of maximum residual, place a bump at that cell centre with s=0.5/N and amplitude equal to that cell height, subtract it, and repeat 15 times (residual clipped at 0). Objective is -log R_of(rasterize(bumps)) computed at full N=84992 with fftconvolve. Optimize with Powell in stages: first the single spike bump's (c, log s, log a) alone (3 params, 400 maxfev), then the 5 largest remaining bumps together, then the 10 wide bumps, then all 16 together; cap each stage at 2 s process_time and repeat the whole cycle until deadline-3 s. Add 2 restarts with the spike centre jittered by +/- 20 cells and log s in [log(0.2/N), log(2/N)]. Return the best rasterized h only if its exact R exceeds R_of(start); otherwise return start unchanged after using the budget on the restarts.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.94125 (stretch 0.94128). Signature: the initial 16-bump fit reproduces the record to within 1e-4 at N=84992 within the first 10 s (proving the basis can represent it), and then the free-centre stage gains >1e-5 by moving the spike and its shoulders off the integer grid. If the initial fit is already 1e-3 below the record, 16 bumps are too few and the track should raise M or switch to a spike+piecewise-linear-plateau parameterization.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is a saturated local max: ~200 first-order, p-norm, beta, prolongation and bump-model experiments on it failed, and every success was a ~1e-5 tweak. All prior moves are first-order gradients (which vanish on the flat plateau) or representation changes that either preserve the exact staircase or destroy the 1-cell spike. I bet on three untried mechanisms: (1) second-order plateau escape via finite steps along near-null Hessian directions; (2) a native continuous-edge block representation seeded from the record, fixing T26's Gaussian-basis failure; (3) a non-staircase mass-preserving 2x prolongation of p0297 followed by the p-norm/beta ladder. Realistic gains are ~1e-5.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a flat local max: the exact-max gradient vanishes on the plateau and all first-order moves stall. The Hessian has near-null directions along the plateau; a finite step along the smallest-|eigenvalue| direction reaches a different plateau point from which polish can gain.
experiments.change: From p0405 (N=84992). (a) Compute g = gradient of -log R at h via existing _fun_grad. (b) Estimate Hv by central differences: for 24 random unit v, Hv ~= (grad(h+eps*v)-grad(h-eps*v))/(2*eps) with eps = 1e-5*||h||/||v||. (c) Form 24x24 A_ij = v_i . Hv_j, eigendecompose, take the eigenvector with smallest |eigenvalue|, map back d = sum coeff_i v_i. (d) For delta in {1e-3,3e-3,1e-2,3e-2,1e-1}*||h||/||d||: h' = clip(h+delta*d,0), rescale, sharp L-BFGS 250 iters, peak polish; keep best true-R. (e) Repeat (a)-(d) from the best until deadline-3s; final sharp polish. Return best only if R > R(start).
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.941250 (stretch 0.94127). Diagnostic: print the 5 smallest |eigenvalues| relative to the largest; if the smallest is <1e-3 of the largest (a genuine flat direction) and a finite step improves R after polish, plateau escape is real; if all eigenvalues are O(1) negative, the record is a strict local max and this line is closed.

experiments.hypothesis: T26 failed because the 16-Gaussian basis cannot represent the 1-cell spike plus plateau (fit 1e-3 low) and Powell at full N is too slow. The native step-function basis with K continuous edges can represent the record exactly (spike = one tiny-gap block) and freeing the edges gives sub-cell DOF the uniform grid lacks.
experiments.change: From p0468 (N=84992). Represent f as K=64 blocks with edges 0=e_0<...<e_K=1 (log-gap params) and heights a_k (log). Rasterize to N=84992 by exact cell-overlap (cumulative sums, O(N+K)), compute exact R via fftconvolve. Seed by segmenting the record into 64 equal-mass blocks (cumulative-sum quantiles); set the block containing the tallest cell to a tiny gap (1e-3 of its mass-width) with height = that cell's height. Optimize (log gaps, log heights) with L-BFGS-B (gaps in [1e-6,0.2], heights in [1e-6,1e4]) for 400 iters, then Powell on the 10 largest-height blocks' (gap,height), alternating until deadline-3s. Rasterize best, run exact sharp+peak polish. Return best if R > R(start).
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.941243 (match), stretch 0.94126. Diagnostic: print R of the seeded 64-block rasterization before optimization; if within 1e-6 of the record the basis is adequate and any gain is from freed edges; if >1e-4 below, raise K or keep the spike as an explicit separate variable.

experiments.hypothesis: p0297 (0.941241, argmax 0.171) is a distinct construction from p0404/p0405 and has never been prolonged off the uniform grid. A mass-preserving non-staircase 2x split creates sub-cell DOF at N=84992 that the exact staircase cannot access, and the p-norm/beta ladder can exploit them.
experiments.change: From p0297 (N=42496). Prolong to N=84992: for each i, h'[2i]=h[i]-d_i, h'[2i+1]=h[i]+d_i with d_i=(h[min(i+1,n-1)]-h[i])/4, clipped >=0 (preserves each pair's sum, not a staircase). Then p-norm ladder p=8,16,32,64,128 (200 log-height L-BFGS iters each) interleaved with sharp polish (150 iters) and peak-window polish (frac 0.1, 150 iters); then beta ladder 1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7 (150 iters each) with exact re-checks; repeat until deadline-3s. If time permits also try the 3x analogue. Return best if R > R(start).

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is saturated: ~44 local/global moves on it, and on its 42496-twin, returned the start unchanged. The real signal is negative and informative — p0476's prolongation dropped R by 8e-2, so p0297's ff plateau is a knife-edge, grid-locked optimum, not a smooth basin. Meanwhile F385 (zero smallest cells + pedestal over the largest zero run) moved p0209/p0457 from 0.941146 to 0.941154 and shifted the ff argmax 0.159→0.572: macro mass relocation, not gradients, moves these constructions. I bet (1) the record cannot be improved by a few long L-BFGS bursts but might by many cheap short ones, and (2) the two sub-record tracks should keep pushing mass relocation, with a randomised tail-pedestal on T27 and an iterated pedestal cascade on T24.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's 10 no-gain generations all used a handful of long (6-8 s) L-BFGS bursts per round; at a knife-edge plateau the chance that one long burst finds a better basin is lower than many short, differently-perturbed attempts. Hundreds of cheap window-local trials sample far more of the near-plateau neighbourhood per unit CPU, and a block L-BFGS of ~40 iterations is enough to exploit a locally-improving perturbation.
experiments.change: From p0405 (N=84992, R=0.941243). Keep the exact R/objective machinery. Main loop until deadline-3 s: (1) pick a random window [lo,lo+w) with w log-uniform in [256, 8192] and lo uniform in [0, N-w); (2) multiply h in that window by lognormal(0, sigma) with sigma annealed over {0.03,0.02,0.01,0.005,0.002} (advance sigma every 40 trials), rescale, evaluate exact R — record the unpolished R; (3) if unpolished R > bestR - 2e-5, run _lbfgs_block on free = [lo-64, lo+w+64) clipped, 40 iters, then accept only if exact R beats bestR by >1e-13; (4) every 25 trials run one global sharp _lbfgs_log (100 iters, deadline-capped) as a drift-correction. Print per 25 trials: trial count, current sigma, bestR, number of accepted perturbations, and the support histogram (mean lo of accepted windows) so we see whether acceptances cluster. Keep the perturbation RNG seeded and print the last accepted window. Return best if R > R(start).
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250 (stretch 0.94127). Diagnostic: if >=5 of ~250 perturbations are accepted and their windows cluster in one support region, that region is the live lever and should get a long dedicated polish next generation; if 0 acceptances at every sigma down to 2e-3, the record is rigid at all scales below 8192 cells and future main-line effort must change the macro shape or the grid, not perturb it.

experiments.hypothesis: T27's own diagnostic (non-staircase 2x split drops R by 8.3e-2, softened split still 4.7e-2) proves p0297's ff peak is an isolated, grid-locked optimum: any sub-cell degree of freedom destroys the razor-flat plateau, so p-norm/beta ladders cannot exploit prolongation. What has never been tried on this argmax-0.171 construction is the one move that did work on the related low-argmax basin p0209: delete the smallest nonzero cells and re-inject that exact mass at the far end, which changes ff's macro shape (and its argmax position) rather than its cell structure.
experiments.change: From p0476 (N=42496, R=0.941241, argmax of ff at 0.171, 6.3% zeros). (a) Soft-threshold sweep: for q in {0.03,0.06,0.10}, replace h by max(0, h - t_q) where t_q is the q-quantile of nonzero heights, then add back *fraction s* of the removed mass as a smooth bump over the far region [0.55N, N) with profiles: constant, linear ramp rising toward index N, half-cosine (zero at both ends, peak in the middle); s in {0.5, 1.0}. Rescale, evaluate exact R for all 18 candidates, print each with its ff argmax position. (b) Take the best 3 candidates by unpolished exact R; for each run: 200-iter sharp global _lbfgs_log, then _lbfgs_block over the bump region +/-128 cells, then p-norm p=8 and p=32 (150 iters each) and a final sharp polish + peak-window polish; accept only true-R gains. (c) If the best beats 0.941241, spend the remaining time alternating sharp global polish and peak-window polish on it. Return best if R > R(start).
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250 (stretch 0.94126) on T27's own scale. Diagnostic: the unpolished R of the ramp-profile candidates and the post-move ff argmax — if the argmax shifts from 0.171 toward 0.4-0.6 while unpolished R falls only 1e-3 to 1e-4 and polishing recovers past 0.941241, macro mass relocation is confirmed as the only live lever on this basin; if all candidates fall >1e-2 and never recover, p0297's shape is globally isolated and T27 should be parked.

experiments.hypothesis: T24's single biggest gain came from exactly one round of 'zero the smallest q, pedestal the largest zero run', which cut zeros 47.7%→14.7% and moved ff's argmax 0.159→0.572. That mechanism was only applied once and only to the largest zero run, with q capped at 0.30. Iterating it (each cycle prunes and re-places mass, then polishes) is the natural continuation, and it keeps changing the macro shape rather than perturbing a saturated local optimum.
experiments.change: From p0457 (N=42496, R=0.941154, 14.7% zeros, ff argmax 0.572). Loop up to 4 cycles until deadline-6 s: in each cycle, for q in {0.10, 0.20, 0.30} zero the smallest q fraction of *current* nonzero cells, take the removed mass M, and distribute it over the largest contiguous zero run with three profiles (constant, linear ramp, tent), sweeping also the choice of run: largest run, and the run with the largest distance from argmax(L). Evaluate exact R for every (q,profile,run) combination and print all; take the best 2 and run _lbfgs_block on (pedestal cells +/- 64) for 150 iters, then a sharp global _lbfgs_log 150 iters; accept the cycle only if exact R improves on the cycle's start, otherwise undo and halve q. After each accepted cycle print R, zero fraction, ff argmax, and Lmax. When the cycle loop ends (or stalls twice), spend all remaining time on the incumbent with alternating p-norm (p=8,32,128) and sharp global polish plus peak-window polish, re-checking exact R each stage. Return best if R > R(start).

plan.analysis: The record is rigid: 11 no-gain generations, and local windows, exact/non-exact prolongation, zero revival/pruning, block models, long polishes and second-order escapes all failed on it. The remaining untried macro lever is the height distribution itself: the record has max/mean 147 and very tall spikes, so capping the tallest cells and redistributing that mass may lower the f*f peak while lifting shoulders. I therefore bet the main slot on a global spike-cap/quantile transform. The bold slot tries a genuinely different construction: solve for f whose autoconvolution approximates a flat target, from p0001. The revive slot re-applies F50's coarse-to-fine logsumexp ladder, but seeded from a heavily downsampled p0478 so the macro shape, not grid-locked spikes, is re-optimized.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f peak is broad but still 18% of knots are within 0.1% of max; its very tall spikes (max/mean 147) may be over-concentrating mass in the peak while leaving shoulders low. Clipping the top height quantile and redistributing the removed mass to the rest of the support is a global shape change not tried on this construction, unlike local perturbations or zero-pruning. It should either reduce f*f Lmax enough to raise R before polish, or prove the spikes are load-bearing.
experiments.change: From p0478 (N=84992). Let h=clip(start,0). For cap fractions f in {0.001,0.003,0.01,0.02,0.05}: on nonzero heights set t=quantile(h,1-f); hcap=min(h,t); removed M=sum(h-hcap). Build three redistributions: (a) add M/N to every cell, (b) add M to the currently zero cells only (if fewer than 10 zeros, to the lowest 1% positive cells), (c) add M as a constant pedestal over the central 50% of support. Rescale each candidate. Evaluate exact R; keep the top 3 unpolished. Polish each with full-support sharp log-space L-BFGS 300 iters, then p-norm p=8 and beta=1e4/1e6 ladders, then a final sharp polish. Keep the best exact R; return it only if it beats the start, else return the start. Print for each cap fraction: unpolished R, polished R, M, f*f Lmax and the 0.1%/1%/5% near-max shares.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250, stretch 0.94127. Diagnostic: if cap f=0.01 or 0.02 gives unpolished R above the start and lowers f*f Lmax, the peak is spike-limited and the polished result should gain; if every cap lowers R and polish returns to 0.941243, the tall spikes are essential and the record must be attacked by a different macro construction, not by height redistribution.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 iff f*f is flat, so a construction driven directly by a flat autoconvolution target may find a basin that gradient polishing from arbitrary seeds misses. Alternating projected gradient on f with a fixed normalized target (flat plateau plus linear ramps) is a genuinely different search from block/height optimization, and can be run cheaply at coarse N then escalated with exact-R polish.
experiments.change: From p0001, start at N=512. Define a target t of length 2N-1: flat plateau of width W centered at N-1 with linear ramps of length Ramp, normalized to L1=1. For W fractions {0.30,0.40,0.50,0.60,0.70} of 2N-1 and Ramp fractions {0.02,0.05,0.10}, minimize J(h)=0.5||h*h-t||^2 with h>=0, sum h=1. Use projected gradient: residual r=(fftconvolve(h,h)-t); grad=2*fftconvolve(r,h[::-1],mode='valid'); step h<-max(0,h-lr*grad); renormalize. Try 3 initializations: ones, a random power-law vector, and a triangular vector. Keep the best 3 target fits by exact R. Prolongate each by mass-preserving interpolation to N=4096, polish exact R with sharp log-space L-BFGS 300 iters, then to N=16384 and polish again, with a short p-norm p=8/32 ladder at N=16384. Return the best exact R found.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.90, stretch 0.93, judged as a new bold track against p0001. Diagnostic: the best target-fit R and exact R at N=512/4096/16384; if exact R rises with N and the resulting f*f has a visibly wider near-max band than 20% of knots, the target-flat inverse construction is a viable new basin even if it does not yet beat the record.

experiments.hypothesis: F50 worked from a trivial constant by rebuilding through a coarse ladder with logsumexp homotopy; the record is grid-locked at N=84992, so starting from a mass-preserving downsample of p0478 to N0=64 and rebuilding upward may escape the spike grid-lock while retaining the record's coarse mass envelope. This is not local perturbation: it forgets sub-64-cell structure and re-optimizes the macro shape at each scale.
experiments.change: From p0478. Mass-preserving block-average downsample to N0=64 (cumulative-mass interpolation). Then run the F50-style ladder for N in {64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192}: at each level run log-space L-BFGS on the exact R objective (300-500 iters), then a logsumexp soft-max homotopy with betas {4,8,16,32,64} and peak-window polish; keep the best exact R and prolongate by mass interpolation to the next level. At N=8192 also try a p-norm p=8 polish. Finally mass-interpolate the best to N=84992 and run a short sharp full-support polish (150 iters) plus peak-window polish. Return the best exact R found; compare against p0478's 0.941243.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250 on this revive track; fallback is to characterize the coarse envelope. Diagnostic: R at N=64/128/256 and whether it climbs monotonically to >=0.94 by N=8192. If the ladder stalls below 0.94, p0478's macro shape is not recoverable from its 64-cell envelope and the record's advantage is genuinely sub-64-cell structure.

info.open_why: Inspect the record program's full code/plan, the T24 pedestal-relocation mechanism that produced the only recent real gain (F385/F373/F152), and F173 which underpins the zero-revival family, to pick a revive most likely to transfer to p0478.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has had ~30 consecutive no-gain generations; every local/gradient/multigrid/bump/sparsity move on it is documented as failing (F288, F407, F413-F415), so slot 1 must be a structural move, not a perturbation. The two deficits of the record's f*f are its ramp ends (only 18% of knots within 0.1% of max vs 43% within 5%). Because R is scale-invariant, mass can be *added* outside the current support for free, changing the ramp geometry — never tested as support extension (F183 revived existing interior zeros only, F373/F385/F409 all removed mass). T29's ladder stalled at 0.867 because it rebuilt from a 64-cell envelope; the informative follow-up is a coarse-grid multistart benchmarked against the downsampled record. T28's 0.7836 came from a crude hand-stepped projected gradient and a centred target; with analytic gradients, asymmetric targets and escalation it can plausibly reach 0.88.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 needs f*f flat; the record's loss comes from the wide ramps at the two ends of f*f, which are set by the tails of f. Since R is scale-invariant, cells can be appended beyond the support with arbitrary small heights (no mass bookkeeping), lengthening/smoothing the f*f ramps and letting the plateau grow; a sweep over extension length and toe profile plus a local re-optimisation of the tail is a structural move that cell-perturbation, zero-revival and 2x prolongation cannot make.
experiments.change: From p0478 (N=84992, R=0.941243). Keep R_of/_fun_grad/_lbfgs_log/_lbfgs_block exactly. (0) Print the contiguous zero-runs (start,len) and the support ends. (1) For ext in {16,64,256,1024,4096} and mode in {left,right,both}: build h_ext (size N+ext or N+2*ext) with the new cells set to a*j-profile: q in {0.5,1,2} means p(j)=a*(1-(j+0.5)/ext)^q, a = r * (mean of the 5% of heights nearest that end), r in {0.01,0.05,0.2,1.0}; evaluate exact R for all combos (cheap with fftconvolve). (2) For the top 6 unpolished candidates run _lbfgs_block on free = the extension cells plus 2*ext cells inward (100 iters), then a global _lbfgs_log (200 iters), accept only on exact-R improvement >1e-13. (3) Separately, one pass filling the interior zero-runs with the same toe profiles (no support growth). (4) Repeat the sweep with the amplitude set annealed (r halved each round, ext fixed to the best two) until deadline-4 s; then one global sharp _lbfgs_log (400 iters) and one beta=300 softmax pass followed by a sharp pass. Return the best array; print the best (mode, ext, q, r) and its unpolished R.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250, stretch 0.941270. Diagnostic: if no extension candidate reaches R0 even before polish and no polish escapes, the support geometry of the record is rigid and the remaining gap is interior plateau shape, not ramp length; if one mode (e.g. right-tail with small a) gives unpolished R0-1e-5 and polish beats R0, the tail is the live lever and gets a dedicated long polish next generation.

experiments.hypothesis: p0487's ladder reached only 0.867 at N=8192 because it rebuilt from a 64-cell envelope, which cannot carry the record's structure. The right question is whether the record's *coarse envelope itself* is optimal: a cheap multistart at N=256/512 benchmarked against the mass-downsampled record answers that directly, and any seed whose coarse R exceeds the record's coarse R is a genuinely new macro shape worth escalating.
experiments.change: From p0487 (start = record, N=84992). (1) Compute the reference track: mass-downsample start by cumulative-mass interpolation to N0 in {256,512}, log-space exact-R L-BFGS (300 iters) at that N0, record R_ref(N0). (2) At each N0 generate 48 seeds: 24 blocky (K~loguniform[3,40] blocks, heights loguniform[1e-2,1]), 8 power-law t^-alpha (alpha in [0.3,0.95]), 8 truncated Gaussians (centre loguniform[0.15,0.85], sigma loguniform[0.02,0.3]), 8 pedestal+sparse-spike (pedestal 0.05-0.3, 4-16 spikes with heights 1-50). Polish each in log space with the exact-R L-BFGS (300 iters; this is fast at N<=512). Print a table of best seed R vs R_ref at each N0. (3) Escalate the top 4 seeds plus the padded record downsample: for N = N0,2N0,...,16384 do mass-prolongation, log-space L-BFGS (300 iters), logsumexp betas {8,32,128} (150 iters each) and a peak-window polish, keeping the best exact R per track; print R per level per track. (4) Mass-resample each of the 5 best to N=84992, run sharp _lbfgs_log (300 iters) + peak-window block polish around the f*f argmax +-300 cells; return the overall best exact R (otherwise the start).
experiments.prediction: Aim: beat the track's 0.8673171 at N=8192 and reach >=0.90 at N=16384; stretch 0.941243. Diagnostic: the per-level table. If a random seed's coarse R exceeds R_ref(256)/R_ref(512), the record's macro envelope is not coarse-optimal and its escalation is the new lead; if no seed ever beats the record's coarse R, T29 is closed and the record's advantage is entirely sub-64-cell (support ends and spike spacing).

experiments.hypothesis: p0484's 0.7836 is limited by its crude hand-stepped projected gradient and by centred, fixed targets, not by the flat-target idea itself (F50/F133 machinery took comparable smooth basins to 0.87-0.88). With analytic gradients through the autoconvolution, asymmetric targets, and a proper escalation ladder, the flat-target basin should climb with N and give a much stronger smooth-basin reference point.
experiments.change: From p0484 (N=4096, R=0.783587). Copy the exact-gradient machinery from p0478 (_knots, _num_and_dq, _backprop, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block) and HARD-CAP every stage with time.process_time() (total <= 56 s; p0484 overran its 60 s budget — never exceed the deadline). (1) Escalation: mass-preserving prolongation to N=8192 then 16384 then 32768; at each level sharp exact-R log-space L-BFGS (400 iters) then p-norm ladder p in {8,32} (150 iters each) then a peak-window block polish on [argmax-0.05N, argmax+0.05N]; print exact R per level. (2) At each level also re-fit the target from the incumbent: minimise 0.5||h*h - t||^2 with the exact residual gradient (grad = 2*fftconvolve(r, h[::-1], 'valid')) by L-BFGS-B in log space, 300 iters, for W fractions {0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7}, ramps {0.02,0.05,0.1} and plateau centres {0.4,0.5,0.6} (t normalised to L1=1); polish each fit with (1) and keep whichever of fit/incumbent has higher exact R. (3) Return the best exact R found (fallback: start). Print the per-level R and the near-max shares (0.1%/1%/5%) of the final f*f.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.85 at N=16384-32768, stretch 0.88 (a smooth-basin construction competitive with F50/F133's 0.87-0.88, far above the track's 0.783587). Diagnostic: whether exact R keeps rising with N and whether the 0.1%-near-max share grows from 1.70% toward 20%+; if the target refit at N=16384 reproducibly wins over plain polish, the asymmetric flat-target family is a viable independent basin and can be escalated toward 0.90 next generation.

info.open_why: Need full detail on T28's flat-target construction (p0484) and T29's ladder revive (p0487) to plan their follow-ups, plus F418/F50 for the flat-target and ladder methods, and F288/p0478 for the record's grid-locked structure.

plan.analysis: The record construction is saturated at 0.941243: 40+ generations of local polish, zero-revival, prolongation, toe-extension and coarse-ladder rebuilds have all returned it unchanged, so the loss lives in the f*f ramps that no local gradient can move. The one mechanism never applied at full resolution is the flat-target inverse fit (F418/F421), which is a different search operator: it changes what is minimised, not the point it starts from. I bet it can reshape the record's ramps while the exact-R polish protects the plateau. Slot 2 continues T28 where p0496 stalled purely from CPU spent on refits, not from a plateau: pure prolongate+polish to 16k-32k is the untested half of its own plan. Slot 3 tries the untried symmetric family on p0234's centred plateau.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's exact-R gradient is flat in the ramp directions because the hard max and the plateau are saturated; minimising ||h*h - t||^2 against a smoothly flattened copy of the record's own f*f gives usable gradient exactly where R's is dead, and starting from the record keeps the plateau that a from-scratch fit (F418/F421, 0.878) never reached.
experiments.change: From p0483 (N=84992, R=0.941243), reuse its _knots/_conv/R_of/_backprop machinery. (1) Rescale h to sum 1; compute L0 = fftconvolve(h,h), M = L0.max(). (2) Build 6 targets t, each normalised to sum 1: t = (L0/M)**gamma for gamma in {0.5,0.7,0.85} and t = minimum(L0, c*M) for c in {0.80,0.90,0.95} (clip the peak, keep everything below). (3) For each target, minimise 0.5*||conv(h,h)-t||^2 in log space (L-BFGS-B on log h, 120 iters, residual gradient 2*fftconvolve(r, h[::-1], 'valid'), hard 6 s cap per target) starting from the record; print exact R of each raw fit. (4) Exact-R polish each raw fit that is within 2e-3 of the record: sharp log-space L-BFGS (300 iters) then beta ladder 1e3/1e4/1e5 (150 iters each) with peak-window block polishes (fracs 0.05/0.15, 150 iters). (5) Spend all remaining time alternating full sharp polish + peak polish on the best, keeping only exact-R improvements; return start if nothing beats it.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.94126 (+2e-5), stretch 0.94130. Diagnostic: the printed (target, raw-fit R, polished R) table; if any flattened target's raw fit polishes to > 0.941243 and its f*f near-max 0.1% share exceeds 18.24%, the inverse-target operator works at full resolution and becomes the main line; if every target's polished R lands at 0.941243 the ramps are a true dead end for shape changes too.

experiments.hypothesis: p0496 ended at N=4096 (R=0.878080) with 55 s used, because its budget went to target refits at the seed level and it never executed its own escalation; the flat-target basin has never been measured above N=4096, so a pure prolongate+polish ladder is the untested half of the idea.
experiments.change: From p0496 (N=4096, R=0.878080), keep its exact_R/_knots/_num_and_dq/_backprop/_fun_grad/_lbfgs_log and p-norm surrogates. Remove every target-refit stage. Ladder: for Nlev in 8192, 16384, 32768: mass-preserving prolongation (np.interp on cumulative mass, or np.repeat+rescale for exact 2x doubling) of the incumbent; then sharp exact-R log-space L-BFGS (400 iters), then p-norm ladder p in {8,32} (150 iters each), then a peak-window block polish on [argmax-0.05N, argmax+0.05N] (200 iters); hard-cap each level with time.process_time() so the whole ladder finishes by 50 s; print exact R and the 0.1%/1%/5% near-max shares per level. If >= 8 s remain after N=32768, run one asymmetric flat-target refit (W in {0.4,0.6}, ramp 0.05, plateau centre at the incumbent's f*f argmax) then polish once more. Return the best exact R with a hard fallback to p0496.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.885 at N=16384 (track best 0.878080), stretch 0.90 at N=32768. Diagnostic: the per-level R table — monotone rise with N confirms a scalable smooth basin (the flat-target family is real and worth escalating towards 0.90+); a drop at 16384 shows the basin is resolution-limited and only target refits, not polish, can grow it.

experiments.hypothesis: p0234's f*f maximum sits at 0.506 of the support (centred), unlike the record's 0.233, so its height profile is close to mirror-symmetric; averaging with shifted mirrors and then optimising inside the symmetric subspace reaches a family (centred flat plateau, symmetric ramps) that no asymmetric local step from it has explored, and with half the free coordinates the polish may converge further.
experiments.change: From p0234 (N=42496, R=0.941230, 6.3% zeros), reuse the record machinery (_conv/_knots/R_of/_fun_grad/_lbfgs_log/_lbfgs_block). (1) For d in {-3,-1,0,1,3} cells and w in {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}: cand = (1-w)*h + w*roll(h[::-1], d), clip>=0, rescale, compute exact R; print each. (2) Take the top 4 by pre-polish R and polish each with sharp log-space L-BFGS (300 iters) plus beta ladder 1e3/1e4 (150 iters each); keep the best exact R. (3) On that best, run a symmetric-constrained polish: half = N//2, parameterise u (first half) in log space, rebuild h as [u, u[::-1]] (odd/even padded), fold the gradient g_half = g[:half] + g[::-1][:half], L-BFGS-B 250 iters. (4) Release the constraint and run the free sharp + peak-window polish to the deadline, keeping the best exact R; return p0234 unchanged if nothing beats it.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record has resisted 14 generations of local levers: target refits (F425), fine-grid mass lifts (F429), toe extension (F419), coarse ladders (F420/F423), full-resolution peak flattening (F428). The one documented blocker is grid-locking: the record's 84992 cells are exactly a staircase doubling of 42496 values, so the fine grid carries no information and its spikes cannot slide or sharpen. Slot 1 attacks that with a deterministic singular-profile lift (f ~ x^{-1/2} at the support ends, the only profile that makes f*f rise instantly to a flat top); slot 2 attacks the same blocker on T30's gauge-equivalent 42496 construction with randomized sub-cell splits, which is the cheap replication. T28's own ladder diagnostic says its basin is resolution-limited (0.87808 -> 0.87850 -> 0.87855), so its remaining lever is strongly-flattened target refits, not more N.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's 84992 cells are a staircase of 42496 values, so every fine-scale degree of freedom is unused and the tall spikes are grid-locked (F407). Lifting to 2x-4x with a *non-staircase* singular profile - mass concentrated in the sub-cell nearest each support end with weights (j+0.5)^-alpha - gives the optimizer, for the first time, a fine-grid initial condition whose spikes can sharpen instead of being flat blocks; exact-R polish on that grid can then exploit the new freedom.
experiments.change: Base p0502 (N=84992, R=0.941243). Reuse its _conv/_knots/R_of/_num_and_dq/_backprop/_fun_grad/_fun_grad_beta/_lbfgs_log/_lbfgs_block/_rescale/_peak_window. (1) h = start; find effective support lo = first index with h > 1e-9*max(h), hi = last such. (2) For s in {2,3,4} and alpha in {0.5,0.75}: build h_s of length N*s; interior coarse cells get uniform sub-weights 1/s (staircase); the cell lo gets weights w_j proportional to (j+0.5)^-alpha with j=0 nearest the support start, and cell hi gets the mirror weights (j=0 nearest the support end); normalise weights to preserve each coarse cell's mass. Also build one variant where the tilt is applied to every coarse cell with h_k > 20*mean(positive h), oriented alternately toward the cell's nearer support end, plus its mirror. (3) Compute exact R of each variant *before* polish and print a table (variant, s, alpha, pre-polish R) - discard any more than 5e-3 below the record. (4) Polish the top 3 variants, each capped by time.process_time(): sharp _lbfgs_log(300 iters), beta ladder 1e3 then 1e4 (150 iters each), then _lbfgs_block peak windows at frac 0.05 and 0.15 (150 iters). (5) If >=10 s remain, run one more full sharp polish on the best and re-time-cap; print, for the final best, the ratio of the first and last 3 sub-cell heights to the local coarse mean before and after polish. Hard-fallback: return start unchanged unless an exact R beats 0.941243. Use ~54 s of the 60 s budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.94126 (+2e-5), stretch 0.94130. Diagnostic: pre-polish R of the tilted variants must stay within ~5e-3 of the record for polish to have a chance; if the polished end sub-cell heights grow >2x relative to the local mean while R rises, the grid-lock was the binding constraint and the same lift should be pushed to 4x. If all variants lose and polish returns to the staircase, grid-locking is not the limiter and the loss sits in the plateau interior.

experiments.hypothesis: p0503 (N=42496, R=0.941232, f*f max at 0.548) has essentially the record's knot statistics (18.25/34.55/42.77 vs 18.24/34.55/42.77), so it is the same shape in a different gauge, and its 42496 grid is cheap enough to lift and re-randomise many times. Random sub-cell splits give an unbiased sample of the fine-structure space that the staircase doubling never visits, and unlike same-grid noise (F417) they add genuinely new degrees of freedom.
experiments.change: Base p0503 (N=42496, R=0.941232). Reuse the record machinery (_conv/_knots/R_of/_fun_grad/_lbfgs_log/_lbfgs_block/_rescale/_peak_window/_make_cb). Loop until the deadline (about 52 s of CPU): (a) lift the current incumbent to 2x with per-coarse-cell random weights drawn from Dirichlet(alpha) over the 2 sub-cells, mass-preserving, alpha drawn per trial from {0.3, 0.7, 1.5} (alpha=0.3 gives very uneven, spiky splits); (b) compute exact R and print it; keep the offspring only if R > track_best - 8e-3; (c) polish the best such offspring with sharp _lbfgs_log(250 iters) then one beta=1e3 pass (120 iters) then a peak-window block at frac 0.06 (150 iters), each stage capped at ~4 s; (d) if the polished R beats the incumbent, replace it (and the track best) and print; else keep the incumbent and draw a fresh random lift. Track and print the best pre-polish and post-polish R seen. Return the best exact R found; if nothing beats 0.941232, return p0503 itself.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.94125 (track best 0.941232), stretch 0.94128. Diagnostic: the spread of pre-polish R tells how much the fine structure costs; if any random split polishes above 0.941232 the fine-grid freedom is real and worth replicating on the 84992 record; if 10+ splits all polish back to the same value, the 42496 staircase already saturates this family's fine structure and T30 should stop chasing resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: p0501's per-level table (0.87808 -> 0.87850 at 8192 -> 0.87855 at 16384) shows its basin is resolution-limited, exactly the branch its own diagnostic flagged: only target refits can grow it. Its g is still domed (7.58% of knots within 0.1% of max vs the record's 18.24%), so the plateau-plus-linear-ramps target family is the limiter; refitting against strongly self-flattened targets (gamma<1 and a clip cap) should raise the top share and with it R.
experiments.change: Base p0501 (N=16384, R=0.878554). Keep its exact_R/_knots/_num_and_dq/_backprop/_fun_grad/_lbfgs_log/_lbfgs_block/prolongate and its _fit_target-style least-squares refit. (1) Compute g = fftconvolve(h,h), normalise by its max. (2) For gamma in (0.6, 0.4, 0.25) and cap c in (0.85, 0.7): target t = clip(g^gamma, 0, c), normalised to sum 1; refit h in log space from the incumbent (<=150 iters, 5 s cap); print exact R and the f*f 0.1%/1%/5% near-max shares and max/mean of the refit. (3) Polish the best two refits with sharp log-L-BFGS (300 iters), a p-norm ladder p in {8,32} (150 iters each), and a peak-window block at frac 0.05 (200 iters), each time-capped. (4) If >=12 s remain, take the best incumbent, prolongate to 32768 (mass-preserving), and repeat steps 1-3 once with the best (gamma, c), then final sharp polish. Keep the best exact R throughout; print a per-level R table. Hard-fallback to p0501 if nothing beats 0.878554. Use ~54 s.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.90 at N=16384, stretch 0.92 after the 32768 escalation (track best 0.878554). Diagnostic: whether the top-0.1% near-max share jumps from 7.58% toward 15-18% and max/mean rises from 57 - if the share rises while R rises, the target family was the limiter and the flat-target basin is scalable; if the refits collapse back to a dome after polish, the smooth family is fundamentally capped well below the record and T28 should be retired as an information source.
